title: Redis: data structures, expiry and persistence

videos.script: Two copies of the bookshop each keep a cache in their own memory. One has the old price, one has the new. Visitors get whichever answers. {{two}} A cache the whole application shares has to live outside every copy of it. The usual place is Redis. {{redis}} Redis is a server that keeps everything in memory. It answers commands, one at a time, in order. That is why a counter in Redis is never wrong. {{order}} And its values are not only strings. A record with fields. A list of what you viewed last. A ranking of bestsellers, kept sorted by the server. {{types}} In this lesson you use each of those, give every value a lifetime, and call Redis from Python. {{python}} Then you fill its memory, and choose what it does when there is no more: refuse, or forget. You crash it, and see what comes back. And you give the application a password that can only touch its own keys. {{limits}}
